title: Michaelis-Menten Kinetics: Rate Saturation and Km

paper.title: The kinetics of the inversion effect of invertase

hook: How fast can an enzyme work? Explore how reaction rate depends on substrate concentration and discover the meaning of Km.

symbols.meaning: Maximum reaction rate at saturating substrate
Michaelis constant: substrate concentration at half Vmax

equation.caption: Michaelis-Menten equation: rate v as a function of substrate concentration [S].

explorations.title: Half Vmax at [S]=Km
explorations.predict: Set [S] equal to Km. What is the rate compared to Vmax?
explorations.observe: The rate v is exactly half of Vmax.
explorations.why: When [S]=Km, the denominator becomes 2Km, so v = Vmax*Km/(2Km) = Vmax/2.

explorations.title: Saturation at high [S]
explorations.predict: Increase [S] to a very high value (e.g., 20) while keeping Km small (e.g., 0.1). What happens to the rate?
explorations.observe: The rate approaches Vmax but does not exceed it.
explorations.why: As [S] >> Km, the term Km in the denominator becomes negligible, so v ≈ Vmax*[S]/[S] = Vmax.

limitation: This model assumes a single substrate, irreversible product formation, and steady-state conditions. It does not account for cooperativity, inhibition, or multiple substrates.
misconception: The rate does not increase indefinitely with substrate concentration; it saturates at Vmax.

claims.text: The Michaelis-Menten equation describes the rate of enzymatic reactions.
At [S]=Km, the reaction rate is half of Vmax.
The rate approaches Vmax as [S] becomes very large.
The interactive curve and table are generated from the equation with user-controlled parameters.

outcomes.outcome: Explain the meaning of Km and its relation to Vmax.
Calculate the reaction rate for given Vmax, Km, and [S].
Describe how the rate changes with substrate concentration and why it saturates.
